attribution: Hanna Köpcke, Andreas Thor, Erhard Rahm. Evaluation of entity resolution approaches on real-world match problems. VLDB 2010. Leipzig Database Group DBLP-ACM benchmark.
limitations: Bibliographic DBLP-ACM cross-source matching only; no claim of universal scholarly coverage.
No independent multi-source/version cluster gold. Separate synthetic functional cases cover transitive bridges and absent/present pages/abstract.

metrics.clusterErrors: Report predicted components spanning multiple oracle components (overmerge), oracle components spanning multiple predicted components (fragmentation), and pair errors induced by transitive closure separately.
metrics.clusterOracle: Connected components of frozen one-to-one gold pairs plus unmatched singletons; derived oracle, not independently labeled multi-source clusters.
metrics.pairPrecision: gold returned cross-source pairs / all returned cross-source pairs; zero predictions=0
metrics.pairRecall: gold returned cross-source pairs / all frozen gold pairs wholly in split
metrics.qualificationDiscipline: Tune only on development. Freeze scoring configuration before reading qualification results; retain every qualification outcome, and disclose later changes rather than silently reusing the holdout.

splitRule: SHA-256 of UTF-8 DBLP-ACM-component-split-v1 + LF + sorted source-qualified component IDs joined by LF; first byte even=development, odd=qualification. Unmatched records are singleton components.
transformations: Original archive retained unchanged in ignored local artifacts; its digest is provenance, not a required test input.
Each CSV losslessly transcoded from ISO-8859-1 to UTF-8, preserving every character and line ending. Reverse encoding reconstructs the exact upstream member bytes and digest.
Source-qualified IDs and component-disjoint splits are derived; gold pairs unchanged.
upstreamCountDiscrepancy: Website lists 2614 DBLP records; frozen archive contains 2616. Raw bytes and actual counts govern this fixture.
